question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the Pythagorean identity

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic Pythagorean identity

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta -{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta =1.
$$

Setting $\theta =1-3x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cosh}^{2}⁡(1-3x)-{sinh}^{2}⁡(1-3x) & =1 \\ {cosh}^{2}⁡(1-3x) & =1+{sinh}^{2}⁡(1-3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the above, we rewrite and calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3}{2+2{sinh}^{2}⁡(1-3x)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{3}{2(1+{sinh}^{2}⁡(1-3x))}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{3}{2{cosh}^{2}⁡(1-3x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\int \frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡(1-3x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\int {sech}^{2}⁡(1-3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(1-3x))+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(1-3x)+C\end{aligned}
$$
